pages.text:
# AI agents

Connect an AI client to the Kofra documentation MCP server so it can search and read these pages, the
API reference and the error catalogue while it helps you. The server needs no login and holds no
account data.

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http kofra-docs https://mcp.kofra.app/docs
```

## The documentation server

| | |
|---|---|
| Endpoint | `https://mcp.kofra.app/docs` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP, stateless; protocol revision `2026-07-28` and 2025-era clients |
| Login | None |
| Tools | `docs_search`, `docs_read` |
| Resources | `kofra://docs/<slug>`, `kofra://openapi`, `kofra://errors/<code>` |

For any other MCP client, add a remote server with the endpoint above and the Streamable HTTP
transport. The list of endpoints is also published at `/.well-known/mcp.json`.

### Tools

- `docs_search`: find pages by words. Takes `query` and an optional `limit` (1 to 20, default 5).
  Answers with ranked matches, each with a `slug`, `title` and `snippet`.
- `docs_read`: read one page by its `slug`. Answers with the page in Markdown.

Both tools only read. They never change anything and never fetch other sites.

### Resources

- `kofra://docs/<slug>`: each documentation page in Markdown, for example
  `kofra://docs/errors/bucket_not_found`.
- `kofra://openapi`: the OpenAPI 3.1 contract of the Kofra API.
- `kofra://errors/<code>`: one entry of the error catalogue as JSON.

## Prompts to try

- "Using the Kofra docs, show me the curl command that creates a bucket."
- "What does the Kofra error `idempotency_key_reused` mean, and how do I fix it?"
- "Which scopes does an API token need to list access keys?"

## The account server

A second MCP server, for managing buckets, keys and usage in your own workspace with your sign-in, comes
later. Until then, use the API with a token.

pages.title: Cancel a deletion
pages.text:
# Cancel a deletion

```sh
curl -sS -X POST 'https://api.kofra.app/v1/account/deletion/cancel' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KOFRA_API_TOKEN"
```

Operation `account.cancel_deletion`: `POST /v1/account/deletion/cancel`.

Cancels a deletion that is waiting for confirmation or scheduled, as
long as `erase_at` has not passed. The account, its buckets and its keys
work again at once.

Scopes: `account:delete`.

## Parameters

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | no | string | Makes a retry safe: the same key and the same request within 24 hours return the first answer. The key is bound to the method, the path, the query and the body of its first request: `dry_run=true` and a request without it (or with `dry_run=false`, which is the same request) are different requests and need different keys. 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters; a UUID is a good choice. |

## Responses

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| 200 | The deletion was cancelled; the account as it is now. |
| 400 | `unknown_field`, `validation_failed` |
| 401 | `token_expired`, `unauthenticated` |
| 403 | `insufficient_scope`, `role_forbidden` |
| 409 | `deletion_final`, `deletion_not_requested`, `idempotency_key_in_use` |
| 422 | `idempotency_key_reused` |
| 429 | `rate_limited` |
| 500 | `internal_error` |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` |

Example `200` body:

```json
{
  "id": "ws_01jd3k9v6q2m8x4t7r5n0b1c2d",
  "state": "active",
  "access": "full",
  "s3_endpoint": "https://s3.kofra.io",
  "limits": {
    "storage_bytes": 1099511627776,
    "upload_24h_bytes": 214748364800,
    "download_allowance_bytes": 1099511627776,
    "active_keys": 20
  },
  "suspension": null,
  "deletion": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-01T09:30:00Z"
}
```

## Error codes

| Code | Status | Retryable | Title |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`deletion_final`](../errors/deletion_final.md) | 409 | no | Deletion can no longer be cancelled |
| [`deletion_not_requested`](../errors/deletion_not_requested.md) | 409 | no | No deletion to cancel |
| [`idempotency_key_in_use`](../errors/idempotency_key_in_use.md) | 409 | yes | Same request is still running |
| [`idempotency_key_reused`](../errors/idempotency_key_reused.md) | 422 | no | Idempotency key used with another request |
| [`insufficient_scope`](../errors/insufficient_scope.md) | 403 | no | Token lacks a required scope |
| [`internal_error`](../errors/internal_error.md) | 500 | no | Internal error |
| [`rate_limited`](../errors/rate_limited.md) | 429 | yes | Too many requests |
| [`role_forbidden`](../errors/role_forbidden.md) | 403 | no | Your role does not allow this |
| [`service_unavailable`](../errors/service_unavailable.md) | 503 | yes | Service is busy |
| [`token_expired`](../errors/token_expired.md) | 401 | no | API token has expired |
| [`unauthenticated`](../errors/unauthenticated.md) | 401 | no | Authentication required |

pages.title: Request deletion of the account
pages.text:
# Request deletion of the account

```sh
curl -sS -X DELETE 'https://api.kofra.app/v1/account?dry_run=true' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KOFRA_API_TOKEN"
```

The example sends `dry_run=true`: the answer shows what would change and nothing changes. Remove it to make the change.

Operation `account.delete`: `DELETE /v1/account`.

Starts a deletion of the whole workspace. The deletion is not scheduled
until a signed-in Owner confirms it in the console: the answer carries
the `confirm_url` to open. Until it is confirmed, nothing changes.

After confirmation every bucket, object and key stops being reachable,
and the data is cryptographically erased at `erase_at`. Until then the
deletion can be cancelled with `POST /v1/account/deletion/cancel`.

Scopes: `account:delete`.

## Parameters

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_run` | query | no | boolean | When `true`, answer `200` with the plan of what would change, and change nothing. |
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | no | string | Makes a retry safe: the same key and the same request within 24 hours return the first answer. The key is bound to the method, the path, the query and the body of its first request: `dry_run=true` and a request without it (or with `dry_run=false`, which is the same request) are different requests and need different keys. 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters; a UUID is a good choice. |

## Responses

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| 200 | Dry run. What the deletion would do; nothing was changed. |
| 202 | The deletion request was created and waits for confirmation in the console. |
| 400 | `unknown_field`, `validation_failed` |
| 401 | `token_expired`, `unauthenticated` |
| 403 | `account_unavailable`, `insufficient_scope`, `role_forbidden` |
| 409 | `deletion_already_requested`, `idempotency_key_in_use` |
| 422 | `idempotency_key_reused` |
| 429 | `rate_limited` |
| 500 | `internal_error` |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` |

Example `202` body:

```json
{
  "status": "pending_confirmation",
  "reason": "customer",
  "requested_at": "2026-11-19T10:00:00Z",
  "confirm_url": "https://console.kofra.app/confirm/del_01jd3m2b7s9k4x6p8r0t1v3w5y",
  "confirm_by": "2026-11-19T10:15:00Z",
  "erase_at": null
}
```

| [`account_unavailable`](../errors/account_unavailable.md) | 403 | no | Account is not available |
| [`deletion_already_requested`](../errors/deletion_already_requested.md) | 409 | no | Deletion already requested |

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"backups"}'

Creates an empty bucket. Bucket names are unique within the workspace.

pages.title: Read the event feed
pages.text:
# Read the event feed

```sh
curl -sS -X GET 'https://api.kofra.app/v1/events' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KOFRA_API_TOKEN"
```

Operation `events.list`: `GET /v1/events`.

Events for this workspace, oldest first, kept 30 days. Start without a
cursor, then pass each `next_cursor`. At the end of the feed
`next_cursor` is the position to poll from next, not `null`. If the
feed was rebuilt, an old cursor answers `feed_reset`.

Event types use `resource.verb_past` names, for example `key.created`,
`key.revoked`, `usage.limit_reached`, `account.suspended`. New types
may be added within `/v1`; ignore types you do not know.

Scopes: `events:read`.

## Parameters

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | no | integer | Items per page, 1 to 200. |
| `cursor` | query | no | string (Cursor) | The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Omit for the first page. |

## Responses

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| 200 | One page of events. |
| 400 | `invalid_cursor`, `unknown_field`, `validation_failed` |
| 401 | `token_expired`, `unauthenticated` |
| 403 | `account_unavailable`, `insufficient_scope` |
| 409 | `feed_reset` |
| 429 | `rate_limited` |
| 500 | `internal_error` |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` |

Example `200` body:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "evt_01jd3n4c8t0m5y7q9s1u3w5x7z",
      "type": "key.created",
      "created_at": "2026-11-19T10:00:00Z",
      "data": {
        "key_id": "KF7Q2M8X4T7R5N0B"
      }
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "ec_7Hq2Lk9P"
}
```

## Error codes

| [`account_unavailable`](../errors/account_unavailable.md) | 403 | no | Account is not available |

# Create an access key

```sh
curl -sS -X POST 'https://api.kofra.app/v1/keys' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KOFRA_API_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"nightly-backup","grants":[{"bucket":"backups","access":"read_write"}]}'
```

Operation `keys.create`: `POST /v1/keys`.

Creates an S3 access key pair with access to the listed buckets. The
secret is in this response only; store it at once. A replay of the same
request with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the key with
`secret_access_key: null`: revoke that key and create a new one if the
secret was lost.

Whoever holds a key with access to a bucket can read its objects, so
`keys:write` is treated as data access. The grants cannot exceed the
caller's own access: a grant on a bucket, or an access level, that the
caller's role does not allow is refused with `role_forbidden`.

Through the MCP tool `keys_create`, the secret is not in the tool
result: the result links to a console page that shows it once.

Scopes: `keys:write`.

## Parameters

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | header | no | string | Makes a retry safe: the same key and the same request within 24 hours return the first answer. The key is bound to the method, the path, the query and the body of its first request: `dry_run=true` and a request without it (or with `dry_run=false`, which is the same request) are different requests and need different keys. 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters; a UUID is a good choice. |

## Request body

`application/json`, required: object (AccessKeyCreate).

```json
{
  "name": "nightly-backup",
  "grants": [
    {
      "bucket": "backups",
      "access": "read_write"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Responses

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| 201 | The key was created. The secret is shown once. |
| 400 | `unknown_field`, `validation_failed` |
| 401 | `token_expired`, `unauthenticated` |
| 403 | `account_read_only`, `account_unavailable`, `insufficient_scope`, `role_forbidden` |
| 404 | `bucket_not_found` |
| 409 | `idempotency_key_in_use`, `key_limit_reached` |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` |
| 415 | `unsupported_media_type` |
| 422 | `idempotency_key_reused` |
| 429 | `rate_limited` |
| 500 | `internal_error` |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` |

Example `201` body:

```json
{
  "id": "KF7Q2M8X4T7R5N0B",
  "name": "nightly-backup",
  "grants": [
    {
      "bucket": "backups",
      "access": "read_write"
    }
  ],
  "created_at": "2026-11-19T10:00:00Z",
  "last_used_at": null,
  "secret_access_key": "EXAMPLEsecretEXAMPLEsecretEXAMPLE0000000",
  "s3_endpoint": "https://s3.kofra.io"
}
```

| Code | Status | Retryable | Title |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`account_read_only`](../errors/account_read_only.md) | 403 | no | Account is read-only |
| [`account_unavailable`](../errors/account_unavailable.md) | 403 | no | Account is not available |
| [`bucket_not_found`](../errors/bucket_not_found.md) | 404 | no | Bucket not found |
| [`idempotency_key_in_use`](../errors/idempotency_key_in_use.md) | 409 | yes | Same request is still running |
| [`idempotency_key_reused`](../errors/idempotency_key_reused.md) | 422 | no | Idempotency key used with another request |
| [`insufficient_scope`](../errors/insufficient_scope.md) | 403 | no | Token lacks a required scope |
| [`internal_error`](../errors/internal_error.md) | 500 | no | Internal error |
| [`key_limit_reached`](../errors/key_limit_reached.md) | 409 | no | Too many active access keys |
| [`payload_too_large`](../errors/payload_too_large.md) | 413 | no | Request body is too large |

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KOFRA_API_TOKEN"

Operation `usage.days`: `GET /v1/usage/days`.

can still change; a `final` day is sealed; an `under_review` day is
being re-checked and may be corrected.

# Idempotency key used with another request

Code: `idempotency_key_reused`
HTTP status: 422
Retryable: no, not without a change

An `Idempotency-Key` is bound to the first request sent with it for 24 hours, that is to its method, path, query and body. The same key with a different method, path, query or body is refused, so `dry_run=true` and the same request without it need different keys (`dry_run=false` and an omitted `dry_run` are the same request).

## What to do

Use a new Idempotency-Key for a different request; reuse a key only to repeat the identical request.

## Example

```http

Content-Type: application/problem+json
Kofra-Request-Id: req_01jd3examplerequestid0000
```

  "code": "idempotency_key_reused",
  "detail": "This Idempotency-Key was first used with a different body.",
  "hint": "Use a new Idempotency-Key for a different request; reuse a key only to repeat the identical request.",
  "docs_url": "https://kofra.app/docs/errors/idempotency_key_reused.md",

pages.text:
# Kofra API conventions

The Kofra API manages a storage workspace: buckets, S3 access keys, usage, the account's state and its
event feed. Object data never goes through this API; read and write objects through the S3 endpoint with
any S3 tool, or with a presigned URL from `POST /v1/objects/presign`.

```sh
export KOFRA_API_TOKEN='...'   # an API token from the console
curl -sS https://api.kofra.app/v1/buckets -H "Authorization: Bearer $KOFRA_API_TOKEN"
```

**Status: draft.** The contract is published ahead of the service.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer <API token>`. A token belongs to exactly one workspace, so paths carry no
workspace ID. Tokens carry scopes such as `buckets:read` or `keys:write`; each reference page names the
scopes its operation needs.

## Errors

Every error is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` body with a stable `code`, a one-sentence `hint`
that says what to do next, a `docs_url`, the `request_id` and `retryable`. Branch on `code`, never on
`title` or `detail`. The [error catalogue](errors/index.md) lists every code.

## Lists

Lists use cursor pagination: `limit` (1 to 200, default 50) and `cursor`. The body has `data` and
`next_cursor`, which is `null` on the last page, and a `Link: <...>; rel="next"` header repeats it.

## Writes

`POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` accept an `Idempotency-Key` header, kept for 24 hours: a retry with the same
key and the same request returns the first answer. Destructive operations accept `dry_run=true`, which
answers with the plan and changes nothing.

## Headers on every response

`Kofra-Request-Id` identifies the request; quote it to support. `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy`
describe the rate limits. `429` and `503` answers also carry `Retry-After`.

## Compatibility within /v1

Unknown request fields are refused with `unknown_field`. Clients must ignore unknown response fields:
new fields are added within `/v1`. Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC. Sizes are integers in bytes, in fields
whose names end in `_bytes`.

## Reference

The [API reference](api/index.md) has one page per operation, each opening with a runnable `curl`
example. The machine-readable contract is at `https://api.kofra.app/openapi.json`.

errors.title: Idempotency key used with another request
errors.hint: Use a new Idempotency-Key for a different request; reuse a key only to repeat the identical request.
errors.meaning: An `Idempotency-Key` is bound to the first request sent with it for 24 hours, that is to its method, path, query and body. The same key with a different method, path, query or body is refused, so `dry_run=true` and the same request without it need different keys (`dry_run=false` and an omitted `dry_run` are the same request).

errors.title: Too many requests
errors.hint: Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then retry; spread requests out to stay under the limit.
errors.meaning: The credential or workspace has used up its request allowance for now. The `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers describe the limit that applied.

errors.title: Internal error
errors.hint: Contact support and quote the `request_id`; repeating the same request is not expected to help.
errors.meaning: The request failed for a reason that is not one of the codes above. No detail of the cause is returned.

errors.title: Service is busy
errors.hint: Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, then send the same request again.
errors.meaning: The service is temporarily busy or a dependency is briefly unavailable. Nothing was changed.

## API reference

- [Create a bucket](https://mcp.kofra.app/docs/api/buckets.create.md): `POST /v1/buckets`: Create a bucket

- [Get a bucket](https://mcp.kofra.app/docs/api/buckets.get.md): `GET /v1/buckets/{bucket}`: Get a bucket
- [List buckets](https://mcp.kofra.app/docs/api/buckets.list.md): `GET /v1/buckets`: List buckets
- [Read the event feed](https://mcp.kofra.app/docs/api/events.list.md): `GET /v1/events`: Read the event feed
- [Kofra API reference](https://mcp.kofra.app/docs/api/index.md): One page per operation. Every page opens with a runnable `curl` example; set `KOFRA_API_TOKEN` to an API token first. Base URL: `https://api.kofra.app`. The contract itself is the `kofra://openapi`...

- [Update an access key](https://mcp.kofra.app/docs/api/keys.update.md): `PATCH /v1/keys/{key_id}`: Update an access key
- [Create a presigned URL](https://mcp.kofra.app/docs/api/objects.presign.md): `POST /v1/objects/presign`: Create a presigned URL
- [List usage per bucket](https://mcp.kofra.app/docs/api/usage.buckets.md): `GET /v1/usage/buckets`: List usage per bucket

- [Get current usage](https://mcp.kofra.app/docs/api/usage.get.md): `GET /v1/usage`: Get current usage
